methods.notes: BLE is the secondary link: the Classic side advertises as "OBDLink MX+" (SPP, UUID 00001101) and is primary per the vendor spec sheet. The app falls back to Classic when an operation requires it (DualModeRequiresClassicBluetoothException).

device.name: OBDLink MX+
device.notes:
Dual-mode Bluetooth OBD-II adapter on an STN chipset (STN2255 on original units — out of production per OBDLink FRPM rev F §3.1; STN2256 on current production, reported). Unlike the BLE-only OBDLink CX, the MX+ leads with Bluetooth Classic v3.0 (SPP + Apple iAP2, so iOS works over MFi) and also exposes a BLE GATT serial pipe — vendor spec sheet lists "Class 1.5 Bluetooth v3.0, Profiles: SPP, iAP2" and the FRPM documents MX+ BLE output. The vendor app carries both a Classic driver and a BLE driver and treats the MX+ as dual-mode (BluetoothLEDevice.IsDualMode, DualModeRequiresClassicBluetoothException in the app's OCTech.OBD2 assembly).
The MX+ is one of only three wireless OBDLink adapters (MX, MX+, EX) that reach Ford MS-CAN (J1962 pins 3/11) and GM SW-CAN / GMLAN single-wire CAN (pin 1) — the `alt_can_bus` capability. That is what tools like FORScan and the vendor's own enhanced diagnostics need for body and chassis modules.
Evidence base: static analysis of the official OBDLink Android app (package OCTech.Mobile.Applications.OBDLink, version 7.4.0, a .NET MAUI app — AOT assemblies recovered from the libassembly-store.so blob and decompiled). All app-derived facts are marked verification: reported until replayed against hardware. Nothing here has been captured from a live adapter. 2026-08-13 confirmation pass: the managed-assembly claims relied on below (FFF0/FFF1/FFF2 GATT UUIDs, the api.obdlink.com firmware endpoints with Stable/Beta branches, the bootloader upload/recovery classes, the dual-mode and pairing-mode strings, and the ST command literals) were all re-verified present in the recovered OCTech.OBD2.dll, OCTech.OBDLink.dll and OBDLink.dll — app-confirmed, not hardware-tested.
SAFETY: as with any dongle, OBD pin 16 is usually unswitched. The MX+ has BatterySaver sleep (< 2 mA claimed) and overvoltage protection, so the vendor says it can stay plugged in — treat that as a claim, not a guarantee, on motorcycles and older vehicles.

credentials.notes: Vendor claims encrypted link ("secure 128-bit data encryption"). The physical button is the proof of possession; an adapter in pairing mode in a public place is pairable by anyone nearby within the window.

factory_reset.effect: Restores the adapter to factory settings (vendor support article 43000714324). Clears adapter configuration and bonds; nothing on the vehicle is touched.

steps.action: Hold the adapter button for 15 seconds, or until the POWER LED flashes rapidly.

methods.description: Press the Connect button on the adapter to open the pairing window, then pair from the host OS Bluetooth settings. Adapter pairing mode is configurable (Auto / Manual) via the vendor app.

steps.action: Plug the MX+ into the diagnostic connector and switch the ignition on.
steps.expect: Green POWER LED on; adapter idle.

steps.action: Press the Connect button on the adapter.
steps.expect: Blue BT LED blinks rapidly; adapter is discoverable for a limited window (about 2 minutes per vendor guides).

steps.action: Pair 'OBDLink MX+' from the host OS Bluetooth settings.
steps.notes: On Android this OS-level bond is required before the vendor app will connect at all (app error string confirms). On iOS the link is MFi Classic (iAP2); BLE is the third-party path.

steps.action: Connect from the client and confirm the command interface with ATI, then STI.
steps.expect: ATI returns the ELM-compatible banner; STI returns the STN identification (chip ID and firmware version) — STI is the reliable discriminator between STN silicon and ELM327 clones.

setup.notes: The MX+ does not accept connections silently: pairing requires physical access to the adapter. Pressing the "Connect" button opens a pairing window (blue LED blinks rapidly, roughly 2 minutes per vendor pairing guides); the user then pairs from the host OS Bluetooth settings. The vendor's own description is "Innovative 'Connect' button — requires physical access to enable Bluetooth pairing" with "secure 128-bit data encryption". The app ships a setup wizard with a dedicated press-the-pair-button step (OBDFusion.Pages.Setup.OBDLink. SetupWizardPressPairButtonPage, _press_pair_button.gif animation — both confirmed in the recovered OBDLink.dll app assembly) and exposes an adapter-side pairing mode setting, Auto or Manual (OCTech.OBD2.Communications.OBDLinkMXPPairingMode, with user-facing OBDLinkAutoPairingModeDescriptionText / OBDLinkManualPairingModeDescriptionText strings — confirmed in the recovered managed DLLs). One app error string shows the Classic-first reality on Android (confirmed in OCTech.OBD2.dll): "A compatible OBDLink MX+ device was not found in the list of connected Bluetooth devices. You must pair your OBDLink MX+ in Bluetooth Settings before connecting to the adapter."

rejoin.notes: Re-pairing is a new button press plus OS pairing. Remove stale bonds on the old host first — a phone auto-reconnecting in the background is the usual cause of "adapter stopped working".

known_limitations:
Dual-mode split is firmware- and host-dependent: vendor documentation leads with Classic v3.0 (SPP/iAP2), and the app can demand Classic for some operations (DualModeRequiresClassicBluetoothException). A BLE-only client should treat Classic-only functions as unreachable until the capture plan confirms what the BLE GATT pipe carries.
Firmware update is in-band over the serial link (vendor bootloader protocol), not a BLE OTA service; interrupting an upload forces the recovery path (power cycle + retry from the device list).

adapter_requirements:
Everything the advanced-stn tier guarantees (see the generic obd2-bluetooth-adapter spec) plus alt_can_bus for Ford MS-CAN and GM SW-CAN — the reason vendor tools name the MX+ specifically.
ST command set confirmed in use by the vendor app beyond the ELM327 baseline: STI (STN ID/version), STIM, STMFR, STPBR, STSLCS and the STSL* sleep/wake trigger family (STSLVL/STSLVG/STSLU/STSLX and variants), plus STNFWv in the firmware-update path — literals re-verified in OCTech.OBD2.dll 2026-08-13 (STIM, STMFR, STPBR, STSLCS, STSLVL*, STSLVG*, STSLU*, STSLX*, STNFWv present; app-confirmed, not hardware-tested). Full STN command reference: OBDLink FRPM rev F (scantool.net).

services.name: Serial Pipe (BLE)
services.notes: GATT family A of the generic adapter spec — the same service the OBDLink CX exposes. All three UUIDs appear as string literals in the vendor app (OCTech.OBD2.dll #US heap) beside ServiceAndCharacteristicPairs.DefaultServiceUUID / DefaultCharacteristicRxUUID / DefaultCharacteristicTxUUID (the SPP UUID 00001101 sits in the same heap), and the app enables notifications via the standard CCCD (0x2902 — GetClientCharacteristicConfigurationDescriptor / GattDescriptorUuids in OCTech.OBD2.dll) with a Notify / Indicate fallback (log literal "RXCharacteristic has Indicate property"). UUIDs, CCCD handling and fallback all re-verified in the recovered managed DLLs 2026-08-13 — app-confirmed, not hardware-tested. Not yet observed on-air from an MX+ — the capture plan covers a GATT discovery dump to confirm the MX+ BLE side matches.
